RectangleCLTArxivV1.exists_duplicateCoor.name: RectangleCLTArxivV1.exists_duplicateCoordinates_comparison
RectangleCLTArxivV1.exists_duplicateCoor.expanded_type:
∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {p q n : ℕ} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ξ : Fin n → Ω → RectangleCLT.Vector p} {δ : ℝ},
  RectangleCLT.BoundedIndependentHypotheses μ ξ δ →
    ∀ (r : Fin q → Fin p),
      Function.Surjective r →
        ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ),
          A * A.transpose = RectangleCLT.covariance μ (RectangleCLT.sumVector ξ) →
            ∃ B,
              B * B.transpose =
                  RectangleCLT.covariance μ
                    (RectangleCLT.sumVector fun i ω => RectangleCLT.Companion.SplitV4.duplicateCoordinates r (ξ i ω)) ∧
                RectangleCLT.gaussianLaw B =
                    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (RectangleCLT.Companion.SplitV4.duplicateCoordinates r)
                      (RectangleCLT.gaussianLaw A) ∧
                  RectangleCLT.Companion.rectangleDistance μ
                        (RectangleCLT.sumVector fun i ω =>
                          RectangleCLT.Companion.SplitV4.duplicateCoordinates r (ξ i ω))
                        B =
                      RectangleCLT.Companion.rectangleDistance μ (RectangleCLT.sumVector ξ) A ∧
                    RectangleCLTArxivV1.gaussianMaximumMean B = RectangleCLTArxivV1.gaussianMaximumMean A

RectangleCLTArxivV1.exists_coordinatePad.name: RectangleCLTArxivV1.exists_coordinatePadding_zero_gap_comparison
RectangleCLTArxivV1.exists_coordinatePad.expanded_type:
∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {p n : ℕ} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ξ : Fin n → Ω → RectangleCLT.Vector p} {δ : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p),
  RectangleCLT.BoundedIndependentHypotheses μ ξ δ →
    (∀ (j : Fin p), RectangleCLT.covariance μ (RectangleCLT.sumVector ξ) j j = 1) →
      ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ),
        A * A.transpose = RectangleCLT.covariance μ (RectangleCLT.sumVector ξ) →
          ∃ B,
            B * B.transpose =
                RectangleCLT.covariance μ
                  (RectangleCLT.sumVector fun i ω =>
                    RectangleCLT.Companion.SplitV4.duplicateCoordinates
                      (RectangleCLT.Companion.SplitV4.coordinatePaddingMap hp) (ξ i ω)) ∧
              (∀ (j : Fin (p + 1)), (B * B.transpose) j j = 1) ∧
                RectangleCLT.pairGap (B * B.transpose) = 0 ∧
                  RectangleCLT.Companion.rectangleDistance μ
                        (RectangleCLT.sumVector fun i ω =>
                          RectangleCLT.Companion.SplitV4.duplicateCoordinates
                            (RectangleCLT.Companion.SplitV4.coordinatePaddingMap hp) (ξ i ω))
                        B =
                      RectangleCLT.Companion.rectangleDistance μ (RectangleCLT.sumVector ξ) A ∧
                    RectangleCLTArxivV1.gaussianMaximumMean B = RectangleCLTArxivV1.gaussianMaximumMean A

passages.claim: Surjective coordinate duplication preserves the actual independent centered bounded array with the same envelope, identical distributions and central symmetry. Every coordinate integral functional is exactly reindexed and every norm functional is unchanged. An actual square covariance factor of the duplicated sum is constructed internally, and its Gaussian law, full measurable rectangle distance and Gaussian maximum mean are exact images/equalities. Standard p+1 padding retains unit variance and makes the actual pair gap zero. The ratio dimensionLog(p+1)/dimensionLog(p) tends to one, including along every actual dimension sequence tending to infinity.
passages.method_variation: The generic operation uses existing actual rectangle-preimage/lift and Gaussian duplication primitives; no Gaussian image or duplicated factor is assumed in the operation theorem. The original factor A is the actual chosen factor of the original covariance. All coordinate and norm moments are covered by arbitrary scalar integral functionals. The logarithmic argument writes dimensionLog(p)=1+log p eventually and uses the actual adjacent-log increment limit; the scalar leaf was developed independently by the spherical-balance child and then kernel-checked within this final module. No lower headline is restated or weakened.
